checks.explanation: The 2024 election concluded without a constitutional crisis (results were accepted and transferred peacefully), but this was a probabilistic ('10% or higher') risk estimate rather than a certain prediction, so a single non-occurrence doesn't cleanly confirm or refute the calibration.
Democrats lost control of the House in the 2022 midterms, as predicted (they retained the Senate).
Confirmed: weak GOP Senate nominees (Herschel Walker in Georgia, Blake Masters in Arizona, Mehmet Oz in Pennsylvania) lost winnable races in 2022, and Democrats retained control of the Senate.
Republicans made notable gains and won the House majority in 2022, while the Senate proved tougher and stayed with Democrats, matching the prediction.
The 2022 generic ballot was roughly in the low single digits favoring Republicans, and Democrats did retain the Senate, consistent with Sacks's threshold framework.
The Dobbs abortion ruling and related GOP culture-war positioning are widely credited with boosting Democratic turnout in the 2022 midterms and preventing an anticipated 'red wave.'
